title: Temple of Vesta
visualBrief: Standing Temple of Vesta at Tivoli: roofless hollow dark-rubble cella with original simplified reticulate masonry patches with real southwest doorway and southeast window, blocked eastern relieving arch, ten surviving pale fluted Corinthian columns on the eastern/southern arc, partial curved entablature/annular coffered soffit and circular occupied podium with short southwest approach. Original simplified Tivoli-style floral capitals and horned skull/swag/rosette frieze; small restraint rods. Neighboring Temple of the Sibyl, restaurant furniture, cliff-retaining structures and landscaping remain separate host context. No restored absent columns, complete conical roof, copied inscription/sculpture or photo atlas.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Exact OSM way/432883964 carriesQ1219688 and agrees with named PMTiles cella building/POI35184804972796. Its approximately9.1m circular footprint identifies the cella, not the whole peristyle. Native anchor12.800822243,41.966639022, heading0/east-south axes; mapped cella center[0.013574854432735428,-0.01091013677570185]. Separate Temple of the Sibyl35184580229500 lies about15m north and remains untouched. Picture-led column ring radius6.25m/podium7.25m, ten surviving columns at approximately-80 through100degrees, doorway southwest and window southeast. Restaurant west/Sibyl north and ordinary pictures support approximate facing, with about30degree uncertainty; doorway/window/arc locations are not separately surveyed map controls.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Ordinary-picture/map estimates: cella radius4.6m/wall0.65m, column ring6.25m, podium radius7.25m, columns6.8m above level occupied floor, partial entablature to7.9m and irregular roofless cella top about7.1m. Door2.2x3.8m, southeast window1.1x1.9m with raised sill, blocked relieving arch3.5m wide. Ten columns, incomplete eastern/southern arc and original simplified relief/coffers; fine inventory, sculptural form, heights and absolute threshold levels remain estimates.
